sanskrit: candanāguruvastrāṇi maṇimuktam anuttamam kāñcanaṃ rajataṃ vajraṃ vidrumaṃ ca mahādhanam
english: Sandalwood, aloe, garments, incomparable gems and pearls, gold, silver, diamonds, and coral — great wealth of every kind.

sanskrit: sa koṭiśatasaṃkhyena dhanena mahatā tadā abhyavarṣad ameyātmā dhanavarṣeṇa pāṇḍavam
english: That one of immeasurable soul, with hundreds of crores of that great wealth, then showered the Pāṇḍava with a rain of riches.

sanskrit: indraprastham athāgamya bhīmo bhīmaparākramaḥ nivedayām āsa tadā dharmarājāya tad dhanam
english: Then Bhīma of fearsome valor, arriving at Indraprastha, reported all that wealth to the king of righteousness.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tathaiva sahadevo 'pi dharmarājena pūjitaḥ mahatyā senayā sārdhaṃ prayayau dakṣiṇāṃ diśam
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: In like manner Sahadeva too, honored by the king of righteousness, marched with a great army toward the southern direction.

sanskrit: sa śūrasenān kārtsnyena pūrvam evājayat prabhuḥ matsyarājaṃ ca kauravyo vaśe cakre balād balī
english: That powerful lord, the Kaurava hero, first conquered the Śūrasenas completely and then forcibly brought the king of the Matsyas under his sway.

sanskrit: adhirājādhipaṃ caiva dantavakraṃ mahāhave jigāya karadaṃ caiva svarājye saṃnyaveśayat
english: He also conquered Dantavakra, lord of lords, in great battle, made him a tribute-payer, and established him securely in his own kingdom.

sanskrit: sukumāraṃ vaśe cakre sumitraṃ ca narādhipam tathaivāparamatsyāṃś ca vyajayat sa paṭaccarān
english: He brought Sukumāra and King Sumitrā under his control, and likewise conquered the western Matsyas and the Paṭaccaras.

sanskrit: niṣādabhūmiṃ gośṛṅgaṃ parvatapravaraṃ tathā tarasā vyajayad dhīmāñ śreṇimantaṃ ca pārthivam
english: The wise hero swiftly conquered the Niṣāda land, the excellent mountain Goshriṅga, and likewise King Śreṇimān.

sanskrit: navarāṣṭraṃ vinirjitya kuntibhojam upādravat prītipūrvaṃ ca tasyāsau pratijagrāha śāsanam
english: Having fully conquered Navarāṣṭra, he advanced against Kuntibhoja; and that king received his command with affection.

sanskrit: tataś carmaṇvatīkūle jambhakasyātmajaṃ nṛpam dadarśa vāsudevena śeṣitaṃ pūrvavairiṇā
english: Then on the bank of the Chamravati he encountered the son of Jambhaka, a king who had been spared by Vāsudeva from among former enemies.

sanskrit: cakre tatra sa saṃgrāmaṃ saha bhojena bhārata sa tam ājau vinirjitya dakṣiṇābhimukho yayau
english: There he engaged in battle with the Bhoja king, O Bhārata; having conquered him in combat, he then marched facing south.

sanskrit: karāṃs tebhya upādāya ratnāni vividhāni ca tatas tair eva sahito narmadām abhito yayau
english: Having received tribute and various jewels from them, he then marched toward the Narmadā accompanied by those very kings.

sanskrit: vindānuvindāv āvantyau sainyena mahatā vṛtau jigāya samare vīrāv āśvineyaḥ pratāpavān
english: The valiant son of the Aśvins conquered in battle the two heroes Vinda and Anuvinda of Avanti, who were surrounded by a great army.

sanskrit: tato ratnāny upādāya purīṃ māhiṣmatīṃ yayau tatra nīlena rājñā sa cakre yuddhaṃ nararṣabhaḥ
english: Then, having taken their jewels, he went to the city of Māhiṣmatī; there that bull among men engaged in battle with King Nīla.

sanskrit: pāṇḍavaḥ paravīraghnaḥ sahadevaḥ pratāpavān tato 'sya sumahad yuddham āsīd bhīrubhayaṃkaram
english: The Pāṇḍava Sahadeva, slayer of enemy heroes, a man of great valor — a very great battle then arose there, terrifying to the fainthearted.

sanskrit: sainyakṣayakaraṃ caiva prāṇānāṃ saṃśayāya ca cakre tasya hi sāhāyyaṃ bhagavān havyavāhanaḥ
english: It was a battle that caused the destruction of troops and placed lives in jeopardy; for the blessed Fire-god, the bearer of oblations, rendered his aid to that king.

sanskrit: tato hayā rathā nāgāḥ puruṣāḥ kavacāni ca pradīptāni vyadṛśyanta sahadevabale tadā
english: Then horses, chariots, elephants, men, and coats of armor were all seen blazing with fire in Sahadeva's army.

sanskrit: tataḥ susaṃbhrāntamanā babhūva kurunandanaḥ nottaraṃ prativaktuṃ ca śakto 'bhūj janamejaya
english: Then the son of the Kuru line became greatly agitated in mind and was unable to offer any reply, O Janamejaya.

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca kimarthaṃ bhagavān agniḥ pratyamitro 'bhavad yudhi sahadevasya yajñārthaṃ ghaṭamānasya vai dvija
english: Janamejaya said: Why, O twice-born one, did the blessed Fire-god become an enemy in battle to Sahadeva, who was striving for the sake of the sacrifice?

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tatra māhiṣmatīvāsī bhagavān havyavāhanaḥ śrūyate nigṛhīto vai purastāt pāradārikaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: It is heard that the blessed bearer of oblations, a resident of Māhiṣmatī, was formerly bound there as an adulterer.

sanskrit: nīlasya rājñaḥ pūrveṣām upanītaś ca so 'bhavat tadā brāhmaṇarūpeṇa caramāṇo yadṛcchayā
english: He had come to be under the authority of the former kings of Nīla's line, wandering there by chance in the form of a brahmin.

sanskrit: taṃ tu rājā yathāśāstram anvaśād dhārmikas tadā prajajvāla tataḥ kopād bhagavān havyavāhanaḥ
english: But the righteous king punished him according to the law; thereupon the blessed bearer of oblations blazed up in anger.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā vismito rājā jagāma śirasā kavim cakre prasādaṃ ca tadā tasya rājño vibhāvasuḥ
english: Seeing him, the king was astonished and bowed his head to the wise one; then Vibhāvasu showed grace to that king.

sanskrit: vareṇa chandayām āsa taṃ nṛpaṃ sviṣṭakṛttamaḥ abhayaṃ ca sa jagrāha svasainye vai mahīpatiḥ
english: The best of those who make excellent offerings granted a boon to that king; and the lord of the earth chose safety for his own army.

sanskrit: tataḥ prabhṛti ye ke cid ajñānāt tāṃ purīṃ nṛpāḥ jigīṣanti balād rājaṃs te dahyantīha vahninā
english: From that time forward, whatever kings out of ignorance seek to conquer that city by force, O king, they are burned by fire here in this world.

sanskrit: tasyāṃ puryāṃ tadā caiva māhiṣmatyāṃ kurūdvaha babhūvur anabhigrāhyā yoṣitaś chandataḥ kila
english: In that city of Māhiṣmatī, O best of the Kurus, the women are said to have become unapproachable in that they follow their own desire.

sanskrit: evam agnir varaṃ prādāt strīṇām aprativāraṇe svairiṇyas tatra nāryo hi yatheṣṭaṃ pracaranty uta
english: Thus Fire granted a boon that women should not be restrained; indeed the women there are svairinis who move about as they please.

sanskrit: varjayanti ca rājānas tad rāṣṭraṃ puruṣottama bhayād agner mahārāja tadā prabhṛti sarvadā
english: And kings shun that kingdom, O best of men, out of fear of Fire, O great king — so it has been from that time forward and always.

sanskrit: sahadevas tu dharmātmā sainyaṃ dṛṣṭvā bhayārditam parītam agninā rājann ākampata yathā giriḥ
english: But Sahadeva of righteous soul, seeing his army terror-struck and surrounded by fire, O king, stood firm like a mountain.

sanskrit: upaspṛśya śucir bhūtvā so 'bravīt pāvakaṃ tataḥ tvadartho 'yaṃ samārambhaḥ kṛṣṇavartman namo 'stu te
english: Then, having touched water and become ritually pure, he addressed the Purifier: "This undertaking is for your sake, O black-pathed one — homage be to you."

sanskrit: mukhaṃ tvam asi devānāṃ yajñas tvam asi pāvaka pāvanāt pāvakaś cāsi vahanād dhavyavāhanaḥ
english: "You are the mouth of the gods; you are the sacrifice itself, O Purifier. Because you purify, you are called Pāvaka; because you carry, you are called Havyavahana."

sanskrit: vedās tvadarthaṃ jātāś ca jātavedās tato hy asi yajñavighnam imaṃ kartuṃ nārhas tvaṃ havyavāhana
english: "The Vedas too were born for your sake, and therefore you are called Jātavedas. It is not fitting that you obstruct this sacrifice, O carrier of oblations."

sanskrit: evam uktvā tu mādreyaḥ kuśair āstīrya medinīm vidhivat puruṣavyāghraḥ pāvakaṃ pratyupāviśat
english: Having spoken thus, that tiger among men, the son of Mādrī, spread kusha grass on the ground according to ritual and sat facing the Purifier.

sanskrit: pramukhe sarvasainyasya bhītodvignasya bhārata na cainam atyagād vahnir velām iva mahodadhiḥ
english: In the sight of the entire terrified and agitated army, O Bhārata, Fire did not pass beyond him, just as the great ocean does not cross its shore.

sanskrit: tam abhyetya śanair vahnir uvāca kurunandanam sahadevaṃ nṛṇāṃ devaṃ sāntvapūrvam idaṃ vacaḥ
english: Fire, approaching gently, spoke these words to Sahadeva, that son of the Kurus, that god among men, beginning with conciliation:

sanskrit: uttiṣṭhottiṣṭha kauravya jijñāseyaṃ kṛtā mayā vedmi sarvam abhiprāyaṃ tava dharmasutasya ca
english: "Rise, rise up, O Kaurava! This was a test I was conducting. I know fully the intention of both you and the son of Dharma."

sanskrit: mayā tu rakṣitavyeyaṃ purī bharatasattama yāvad rājño 'sya nīlasya kulavaṃśadharā iti īpsitaṃ tu kariṣyāmi manasas tava pāṇḍava
english: "But this city must be protected by me, O best of the Bhāratas, so long as the lineage-holders of this king Nīla endure — yet I shall fulfil the desire of your heart, O Pāṇḍava."

sanskrit: tata utthāya hṛṣṭātmā prāñjaliḥ śirasānataḥ pūjayām āsa mādreyaḥ pāvakaṃ puruṣarṣabhaḥ
english: Then that bull among men, the son of Mādrī, rose up with a gladdened heart, and with joined palms and bowed head, he worshipped the Purifier.

sanskrit: pāvake vinivṛtte tu nīlo rājābhyayāt tadā satkāreṇa naravyāghraṃ sahadevaṃ yudhāṃ patim
english: When the Purifier withdrew, King Nīla then came forward and honored with hospitality Sahadeva, that tiger among men, that lord of warriors.

sanskrit: pratigṛhya ca tāṃ pūjāṃ kare ca viniveśya tam mādrīsutas tataḥ prāyād vijayī dakṣiṇāṃ diśam
english: Having accepted that hospitality and placed him under tribute, the son of Mādrī then marched victoriously toward the southern direction.

sanskrit: traipuraṃ sa vaśe kṛtvā rājānam amitaujasam nijagrāha mahābāhus tarasā potaneśvaram
english: Having brought the king of Tripura under his sway and swiftly subdued the lord of Potana, that long-armed hero,

sanskrit: āhṛtiṃ kauśikācāryaṃ yatnena mahatā tataḥ vaśe cakre mahābāhuḥ surāṣṭrādhipatiṃ tathā
english: that great-armed hero, with great effort, then brought Ahriti and Kaushikācharya under his sway, and likewise the lord of Surashtra.

sanskrit: surāṣṭraviṣayasthaś ca preṣayām āsa rukmiṇe rājñe bhojakaṭasthāya mahāmātrāya dhīmate
english: And while dwelling in the territory of Surashtra, he sent envoys to King Rukmiṇī, the wise high minister stationed at Bhojakat.

sanskrit: bhīṣmakāya sa dharmātmā sākṣād indrasakhāya vai sa cāsya sasuto rājan pratijagrāha śāsanam
english: To Bhīṣmaka himself, the righteous soul, who was a direct ally of Indra — he and his son, O king, accepted his command.

sanskrit: prītipūrvaṃ mahābāhur vāsudevam avekṣya ca tataḥ sa ratnāny ādāya punaḥ prāyād yudhāṃ patiḥ
english: That long-armed lord of warriors, glancing affectionately toward Vāsudeva, then took those jewels and marched on again.

sanskrit: tataḥ śūrpārakaṃ caiva gaṇaṃ copakṛtāhvayam vaśe cakre mahātejā daṇḍakāṃś ca mahābalaḥ
english: Then that one of great splendor and immense power brought under his sway the region of Śūrpāraka and the clan called Upakrita, and also the Daṇḍakas.

sanskrit: sāgaradvīpavāsāṃś ca nṛpatīn mlecchayonijān niṣādān puruṣādāṃś ca karṇaprāvaraṇān api
english: And the kings who dwelt on ocean islands, born of barbarian lineage, the Niṣadhas, the Purushadānas, and even those who use their ears as coverings —

sanskrit: ye ca kālamukhā nāma narā rākṣasayonayaḥ kṛtsnaṃ kollagiriṃ caiva muracīpattanaṃ tathā
english: and those men called Kalamukhās born of Rākṣasa stock, and the entire mountain Kollagiri, and the city of Murachi —

sanskrit: dvīpaṃ tāmrāhvayaṃ caiva parvataṃ rāmakaṃ tathā timiṃgilaṃ ca nṛpatiṃ vaśe cakre mahāmatiḥ
english: and the island called Tamra, and the mountain Ramaka — the great-minded hero brought all these under his sway, along with the king Timingila.

sanskrit: ekapādāṃś ca puruṣān kevalān vanavāsinaḥ nagarīṃ saṃjayantīṃ ca picchaṇḍaṃ karahāṭakam dūtair eva vaśe cakre karaṃ cainān adāpayat
english: One-footed men who dwelt solely in the forests, the city of Sanjayanti, Picchhanda, and Karahataka — these he brought under his sway merely through envoys and made them pay tribute.

sanskrit: pāṇḍyāṃś ca draviḍāṃś caiva sahitāṃś coḍrakeralaiḥ andhrāṃs talavanāṃś caiva kaliṅgān oṣṭrakarṇikān
english: The Pandyas and the Dravidians together with the Udras and Keralas, the Andhras and the Talavanas, the Kaliṅgas and the Oshthakarnikas —

sanskrit: antākhīṃ caiva romāṃ ca yavanānāṃ puraṃ tathā dūtair eva vaśe cakre karaṃ cainān adāpayat
english: Antakhi and Roma and likewise the city of the Yavanas — these too he brought under his sway merely through envoys and made them pay tribute.

sanskrit: bharukacchaṃ gato dhīmān dūtān mādravatīsutaḥ preṣayām āsa rājendra paulastyāya mahātmane vibhīṣaṇāya dharmātmā prītipūrvam ariṃdamaḥ
english: The wise subduer of enemies, that righteous soul, son of Mādravatī, having gone to Bharukaccha, sent envoys with affection to the great-souled Vibhīṣaṇa of the Paulastya line, O king of kings.

sanskrit: sa cāsya pratijagrāha śāsanaṃ prītipūrvakam tac ca kālakṛtaṃ dhīmān anvamanyata sa prabhuḥ
english: And he accepted his command with affection; the wise lord also approved that which time had wrought.

sanskrit: tataḥ saṃpreṣayām āsa ratnāni vividhāni ca candanāgurumukhyāni divyāny ābharaṇāni ca
english: Then Vibhīṣaṇa sent various jewels, foremost among which were sandalwood and aloe, and divine ornaments as well,

sanskrit: vāsāṃsi ca mahārhāṇi maṇīṃś caiva mahādhanān nyavartata tato dhīmān sahadevaḥ pratāpavān
english: and garments of great worth and gems of immense value. Then the wise and valiant Sahadeva turned back.

sanskrit: evaṃ nirjitya tarasā sāntvena vijayena ca karadān pārthivān kṛtvā pratyāgacchad ariṃdamaḥ
english: Having thus conquered by force, by conciliation, and by victory, and having made kings into tribute-payers, that subduer of enemies returned.

sanskrit: dharmarājāya tat sarvaṃ nivedya bharatarṣabha kṛtakarmā sukhaṃ rājann uvāsa janamejaya
english: Having reported everything to the king of righteousness, O bull of the Bhāratas, he who had accomplished his task dwelt in happiness, O king Janamejaya.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca nakulasya tu vakṣyāmi karmāṇi vijayaṃ tathā vāsudevajitām āśāṃ yathāsau vyajayat prabhuḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: I shall now tell of the deeds and victories of Nakula, and how that lord conquered the direction that Vāsudeva had won.

sanskrit: niryāya khāṇḍavaprasthāt pratīcīm abhito diśam uddiśya matimān prāyān mahatyā senayā saha
english: Marching out from Khāṇḍavaprastha and heading toward the western direction, the wise one advanced with a great army.

sanskrit: siṃhanādena mahatā yodhānāṃ garjitena ca rathanemininādaiś ca kampayan vasudhām imām
english: With the great lion-roar of warriors, with their battle-shouts, and with the rumbling sound of chariot-wheels, he made this earth tremble.

sanskrit: tato bahudhanaṃ ramyaṃ gavāśvadhanadhānyavat kārttikeyasya dayitaṃ rohītakam upādravat
english: Then he advanced upon Rohitaka, a beautiful and wealthy land rich in cattle, horses, and grain, beloved of Kārttikeya.

sanskrit: tatra yuddhaṃ mahad vṛttaṃ śūrair mattamayūrakaiḥ marubhūmiṃ ca kārtsnyena tathaiva bahudhānyakam
english: There a great battle took place with the heroic Mattamayurakas; and he likewise conquered the entire desert region and Bahudhanyaka.

sanskrit: śairīṣakaṃ mahecchaṃ ca vaśe cakre mahādyutiḥ śibīṃs trigartān ambaṣṭhān mālavān pañcakarpaṭān
english: That one of great splendor brought Shairishaka and Mahichchha under his sway, along with the Śibis, the Trigartas, the Ambaṣṭhas, the Mālavas, and the Panchakarpaṭas.

sanskrit: tathā madhyamikāyāṃś ca vāṭadhānān dvijān atha punaś ca parivṛtyātha puṣkarāraṇyavāsinaḥ
english: Likewise the people of Madhyamika and the Vatadhanā brahmins, and then turning back, those who dwelt in the Puṣkara forest.

sanskrit: gaṇān utsavasaṃketān vyajayat puruṣarṣabhaḥ sindhukūlāśritā ye ca grāmaṇeyā mahābalāḥ
english: That bull among men conquered the clans called Utsavasanketa, and the mighty Gramaneyas who dwelt along the banks of the Sindhu.

sanskrit: śūdrābhīragaṇāś caiva ye cāśritya sarasvatīm vartayanti ca ye matsyair ye ca parvatavāsinaḥ
english: And the Śūdra and Abhira clans, those who subsist near the Sarasvatī, those who live by fishing, and those who dwell in the mountains —

sanskrit: kṛtsnaṃ pañcanadaṃ caiva tathaivāparaparyaṭam uttarajyotikaṃ caiva tathā vṛndāṭakaṃ puram dvārapālaṃ ca tarasā vaśe cakre mahādyutiḥ
english: the entire Pañcanada, and likewise the western territory, Uttarajyotika, the city of Vrindataka, and Dvarapala — all these that one of great splendor swiftly brought under his sway.

sanskrit: ramaṭhān hārahūṇāṃś ca pratīcyāś caiva ye nṛpāḥ tān sarvān sa vaśe cakre śāsanād eva pāṇḍavaḥ
english: The Ramathas, the Harahunas, and whatever kings of the western regions — all of these the Pāṇḍava brought under his sway through his mere command.

sanskrit: tatrasthaḥ preṣayām āsa vāsudevāya cābhibhuḥ sa cāsya daśabhī rājyaiḥ pratijagrāha śāsanam
english: While dwelling there, the mighty one sent a message to Vāsudeva; and he accepted his command with ten kingdoms.

sanskrit: tataḥ śākalam abhyetya madrāṇāṃ puṭabhedanam mātulaṃ prītipūrveṇa śalyaṃ cakre vaśe balī
english: Then the powerful hero went to Śākala, the great city of the Madras, and with affection brought his maternal uncle Śalya under his sway.

sanskrit: sa tasmin satkṛto rājñā satkārārho viśāṃ pate ratnāni bhūrīṇy ādāya saṃpratasthe yudhāṃ patiḥ
english: Honored in turn by that king, as one deserving of honor, O lord of the people, the lord of warriors took abundant jewels and set out again.

sanskrit: tataḥ sāgarakukṣisthān mlecchān paramadāruṇān pahlavān barbarāṃś caiva tān sarvān anayad vaśam
english: Then he brought under his sway the exceedingly fierce barbarians dwelling in the belly of the ocean, the Pahlavas and the Barbaras, all of them.

sanskrit: tato ratnāny upādāya vaśe kṛtvā ca pārthivān nyavartata naraśreṣṭho nakulaś citramārgavit
english: Then, having taken jewels and having brought the kings under his sway, that best of men, Nakula, skilled in wondrous ways, turned back.

sanskrit: karabhāṇāṃ sahasrāṇi kośaṃ tasya mahātmanaḥ ūhur daśa mahārāja kṛcchrād iva mahādhanam
english: Ten thousand camels carried the treasury of that great-souled hero, O great king — immense wealth, as though with difficulty.

sanskrit: indraprasthagataṃ vīram abhyetya sa yudhiṣṭhiram tato mādrīsutaḥ śrīmān dhanaṃ tasmai nyavedayat
english: Then the glorious son of Mādrī, coming to the hero Yudhiṣṭhira who had returned to Indraprastha, presented that wealth to him.

sanskrit: evaṃ pratīcīṃ nakulo diśaṃ varuṇapālitām vijigye vāsudevena nirjitāṃ bharatarṣabhaḥ
english: Thus Nakula, that bull of the Bhāratas, conquered the western direction, guarded by Varuṇa, which had previously been won by Vāsudeva.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca rakṣaṇād dharmarājasya satyasya paripālanāt śatrūṇāṃ kṣapaṇāc caiva svakarmaniratāḥ prajāḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Through the protection of the king of righteousness, through the upholding of truth, and through the destruction of enemies, the subjects were devoted to their own duties.

sanskrit: balīnāṃ samyag ādānād dharmataś cānuśāsanāt nikāmavarṣī parjanyaḥ sphīto janapado 'bhavat
english: Through the proper collection of revenue from the powerful and through governance in accordance with righteousness, the rain-cloud showered as desired and the realm became prosperous.

sanskrit: sarvārambhāḥ supravṛttā gorakṣaṃ karṣaṇaṃ vaṇik viśeṣāt sarvam evaitat saṃjajñe rājakarmaṇaḥ
english: All undertakings proceeded well — the tending of cattle, agriculture, and trade; all of this in particular arose from the activity of the king.
